messages:
alex: kicking off py/ts SDK publish in the change window now. canary has 'stability' flag set to true for a short run. please DO NOT pin yet — holding pins until post-smoke. :shipit:
deploy-bot: CI jobs queued: py-publish-canary, ts-publish-canary, wheels-signing. status updates in thread.
ci-bot: py-publish-canary started (job 8421). uploading artifacts to staging.
maria: saw a failure in the Windows wheel build, looks like a checksum mismatch on zip. investigating. :warning:
jamal: rollback criteria reminder: if >2 unrelated smoke tests fail OR any signature/checksum mismatch on signed artifacts -> immediate unpublish + rollback. we should be strict for signed packages.
alex: acknowledged. if signing fails we untag and reupload signed wheel only. i'll prepare rollback steps in repo ops doc.
maria: quick findings: the wheel was built with older buildx, pip tag differs. re-running build with pinned buildx version now.
ci-bot: rerun triggered by maria (job 8424).
tara: small note for release notes: deprecating the legacy sync client in next stable. draft blurb: "The sync client will be deprecated in the next stable release. Migrate to the async client — see migration guide at https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/migrate-sync-to-async." can someone sanity-check wording?
sean: lgtm. add an explicit timeline: 30 days to migrate + pinning window for critical customers. i'll prep customer comms once we confirm publish time.
maria: re-run succeeded, checksum/signatures look good. wheels signing job passed.
jamal: given that, we can proceed to finalize canary. still hold pins until we run a quick production smoke on dedicated infra (5m test).
alex: running dedicated infra smoke now. will post results within 10m.
deploy-bot: dedicated-smoke started on us-west-2 (smoke-357). logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/357
alex: smoke passed (latency and basic auth tests). moving to final publish step in ~5m. leaving thread for any last objections.
tara: thumbs up from docs — migration guide updated and linked. also added deprecation note to changelog.
jamal: final ask: add a short note to the package description on PyPI/NPM pointing to migration guide and the deprecation timeline. avoid surprising enterprise customers.
alex: will do the PyPI/NPM metadata update after publish. plan: publish canary now, wait 1h, promote to stable if no regression. pin holdback window = 1 week before force-deprecation.
sean: ok, comms plan scheduled. i'll ping support to standby for any pin requests.
deploy-bot: py-publish-canary succeeded. ts-publish-canary succeeded. artifacts available in staging.
alex: published canary. delaying stable promotion for 1h as planned. final note: if any post-canary regression appears, we revert canary tag and unpublish bad artifacts, then follow rollback doc. thanks all. :tada:
